references.text: God promises to meet Moses at the testimony (the ark of the covenant), which corresponds to 'before the testimony' in Exodus 30:36
The comparison passage for the tent of meeting where God will meet the Israelites uses the same expression 'אִוָּעֵד' (I will meet)
The incense altar is placed before the curtain that is in front of the testimony, where God will meet Moses
Description of the testimony and the Most Holy Place, relating to the term 'most holy' (קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים)
The incense altar is described as 'most holy to the Lord', the same designation used for the incense in verse 36
The Lord appears in the cloud above the mercy seat on the testimony, connected to the meeting place before the testimony
Fine-ground incense is mentioned in connection with the grain offering, parallel to the fine-ground incense
The testimony in the tent of meeting as the meeting place between God and Moses
Both verses establish the identical placement of holy objects (the ark and the incense) before the testimony as a condition for God's meeting with the people.
Both verses link a specific liturgical action (burnt offering and incense) to the same theological promise that God will meet His people at the designated place.
The verses illuminate each other by defining the holy zone: the ark contains the testimony, while the incense is to be placed before it as a sign of God's presence.
The verses illuminate each other by outlining the holy zone: the testimony is inside the ark, while the incense is to be placed before it as a sign of God's presence.
The verses compare the arrangement of the tent of meeting's central elements (the ark and the curtain) with the placement of the incense before them.
